column1: # Reviewed over-blocking exclusions for the NWL2020 slur purge.
# One word per line: word, reason. Every entry is present in
# nwl2020-purged.txt and is deliberately NOT denied by this game.
# The test is narrow on purpose: a word is held back only when its
# primary sense in ordinary modern English is neutral, so a player
# could reasonably type it with no idea of the other reading. A word
# that is merely dated, coarse, or contested is still denied.
# The asymmetry that settles the borderline cases: leaving a slur
# valid rewards a player for typing it, while denying an ordinary
# word only makes the game look like it has a small vocabulary. So
# the bar to hold a word back is a genuinely neutral primary sense,
# not a neutral sense that exists somewhere.
# NASPA had already done most of this review. The five words this
# game must not deny (nip, nips, niggard, spade, coot) are absent
# from the source list entirely, which is a large part of why this
# source was chosen over a generic profanity list. src/data/
# slurDenylist.test.ts asserts all five stay accepted and scored.
# Held back but NOT here, and why they stay denied: hebe (the shrub
# genus is real but niche in a US lexicon, and the slur reading is
# live), goy and goyim (used neutrally by many Jewish speakers, but
# NASPA judged them personally applicable), chola and cholo and
# gringo and gringa (self-identifiers in some communities, mild in
# others), redneck and girlies (informal, but the offensive sense is
# the primary one). Each is a judgment call, and each is Antoine's
# to overturn by adding a line here.
